proposals.evidence: DEDR 5041 explicitly records Gondi mūrā/mura ‘cow’, although southern comparanda denote bullocks or buffaloes. The survey mūra ‘cow’ agrees with the Gondi-specific sense; neither animal sex nor species is silently changed.

proposals.evidence: DEDR 4910 gives Gondi mūnju and munj ‘monkey’, with dialect-specific black-faced/langur senses. The survey munju matches the printed complete noun; its generic monkey gloss is retained without adding an unsupported species identification.

proposals.evidence: DEDR 3291 directly gives Maria/Koya Gondi unj- ‘sleep’, beside hunj-/sunj- in other dialects. The survey unj matches the simple zero-initial verb; it is not treated as a causative put-to-sleep formation.

proposals.evidence: DEDR 3115 explicitly gives Gondi taḍmī ‘fire’ (SR.), alongside taṛmi ‘burning coal, ember’. The survey taḍmi matches the fire attestation; the article’s possible connection with DEDR 276 and questioned Kui forms remains unasserted.
